title: Definite integrals of standard forms
what_it_asks: You get a short integrand such as $\frac{1}{ax+b}$, $(ax+b)^{-2}$ or a power of $x$ like $x^{1/2}$, with limits. It is sometimes written as the limit of a sum. You must integrate it, substitute the limits and give an exact simplified value. The idea is to rewrite the integrand as a power or standard form, integrate with the correct factor, then take upper minus lower.
typical_structure: Usually one or two parts. The whole question is typically about 5 or 6 marks, and a single part is often 2 to 4 marks. Sometimes an early part sets up the integral or a limit of a sum, and a later part uses "hence" or "show that" to reach an exact printed or simplified value. Some questions are a single short evaluation.
mark_pattern: The usual part is a 2-mark M1 A1. The M1 is for integrating to the right type of term, and the A1 is for the correct exact result. Longer parts run M1 A1 dM1 A1, or M1 A1 M1 ddM1 A1. There the first M1 A1 is the integration, the next method mark is for substituting both limits and subtracting, and the later dependent marks are for combining the result, for example with log laws or by rationalising. Show-that parts end in a starred A1 that needs a clean route. A B1 sometimes appears for a stated rewrite or value.

where_marks_leak.text: With negative or fractional powers you divide by the old power, multiply instead, or add 1 wrongly. The first M1 goes, and the A1 and any dM1 that depend on it go too.
When the exact value has a surd denominator, you multiply by the wrong conjugate or only change the numerator. The method mark for simplifying is lost, and so is the final A1.
You give a rounded decimal or the wrong number of figures when the question wanted a specific form. The final A1 is lost, even if all the method was right.
You work out $F(\text{lower}) - F(\text{upper})$, or slip on the sign with a negative limit. The substitution method mark is lost, and the A1 after it goes too.
You leave a calculator decimal where a surd, fraction or $\ln$ was asked for. The final A1 is lost.

write_to_earn: Rewrite roots and reciprocals as powers of $x$ on their own line before integrating.
For $(ax+b)^n$ and $\frac{1}{ax+b}$, write the integrated form with the $\frac{1}{a}$ factor, so the integration marks are secure.
Write the substitution as $F(\text{upper}) - F(\text{lower})$ with brackets before you evaluate, especially with negative limits.
Keep surds and logs exact, and combine logs with the laws before giving the final value.
On a show-that, write the line just before the printed result, then the result itself.
